source: master session 2026-08-17 — v0.4.0 release and first live deploy

lessons.title: Wrangler OAuth lands on whatever browser session auto-approves — pin the browser before blaming the login
lessons.problem: Repeated `wrangler login` / `wrangler auth create` attempts kept binding to the wrong Cloudflare account. The consent step never appeared because the DEFAULT browser held a session for a different user, and Cloudflare auto-approves a previously authorized client.
method: Never let wrangler auto-open the browser for account-sensitive auth. Use `--browser=false` and take the printed URL yourself.
Before authorizing, verify which account the target browser session actually holds: open dash.cloudflare.com and read the account ID in the redirect URL.
Complete the consent form only where the intended user is logged in, and read the account name on the consent card before clicking Authorize.
After auth, prove it: `wrangler whoami` must show the expected account ID. An email alone is not proof — one person can hold multiple Cloudflare users.
Bind the profile to the working directories (`wrangler auth activate <profile> <dir>`) so future deploys cannot silently use the wrong default.
signals_it_applies: whoami shows a different account than the one owning the target zone
OAuth completes suspiciously fast with no visible consent screen
the same login flow was already retried and produced the same wrong account
hard_nos: Do not deploy to whatever account is active just because credentials work
Do not retry the identical login flow expecting a different account
Do not create a broad master API token as a workaround
lessons.evidence: cloudflare-ops-mcp v0.4.0 deploy, 2026-08-17: two failed same-flow logins, then --browser=false + verified browser session produced the correct account on the first try; live /health confirmed 0.4.0.

lessons.title: A deploy is done when the live URL says so, not when the tool exits 0
lessons.problem: Upload success and exit codes do not prove the public route serves the new version.
method: After deploy, fetch the live health/version endpoint over the public hostname and compare the reported version to the release.
Exercise one authenticated-failure path to confirm the service fails closed.
Only then report the deploy as complete, quoting what the live response actually said.
hard_nos: Do not report success from a build log alone
Do not test only the workers.dev URL when a custom route is the real front door
lessons.evidence: cfops.nothingunseen.com/health returned version 0.4.0 with the 5 new agent tools; unauthenticated MCP call returned -32001 unauthorized.

lessons.title: Scan the staged diff for secret patterns before every public push
lessons.problem: A public repo push distributes everything staged; a stray key in a config or stash file becomes public history.
method: Scan `git diff --cached` for known secret shapes (API keys, bearer tokens, provider prefixes) before committing.
Keep private operator files under an ignored path and verify the ignore actually excluded them in `git status`.
Store operator secrets outside the repo and reference their location, never their value.
hard_nos: Do not commit local-stashes content, even redacted, without explicit review
Do not paste secret values into commit messages, docs, or vault entries
lessons.evidence: v0.4.0 release: staged-diff pattern scan clean; operator.json confirmed ignored; secret values live only in ~/.amh-secrets and Worker secret bindings.

note: Redacted lesson entry. No OAuth records, connector keys, secret values, raw source bodies, client IPs, or cookies.
